Thanks for the detail and the attachment — the scope is clear. We're prepared to execute a two-part zeroization:

1) Standard retention purge: items older than 90 days (automated retention job).
2) Ad-hoc obliteration: 30-day window records you flagged (manual, one-off zeroization).

High-level timeline: we can start the manual obliteration on Monday (2026-12-21) and expect completion within 24-48 hours, subject to a brief maintenance window for coordination with your engineering/security team.

Evidence package we'll provide after completion:
- Audit stub (PDF) with job IDs, time stamps, and operator IDs.
- Object-level manifest (list of S3 keys removed or tombstoned).
- CRC checksums for destroyed artifacts where applicable.
- Internal runbook excerpt showing the steps executed and any fallbacks used.

I will coordinate the internal SOP and send you an example confirmation email that ClearLine can include in its control records.

One technical note: "obliteration" for some internal caches (hot KV cache snapshots) is performed by cryptographic zeroization of the local cache shards and then invalidation of manifests so nothing rehydrates. For persisted logs in the analytics index we will perform permanent deletion followed by index compaction. Both steps are recorded in the audit stub.

I'll assign Laura to draft the customer-facing confirmation note and Naomi to produce the audit stub. Marcus will run the ops job.

Best,
Priyom
